review.core_challenge: Creating a truthful middle-tier Codex workflow that borrows the local heavy system's planning and validation discipline without becoming a disguised campaign orchestrator or importing unsupported runtime assumptions.
assumptions_to_verify: V1's .claude/archon/plans/ path convention will remain stable through S1 — confirmed by Section 6.6 and design doc §12 Slice 1
Archon's loop schema does not yet support structured loop decisions — stated in PRD Section 9 and design doc §12 Slice 3, not verified against loop.ts
$ARTIFACTS_DIR/e2e-reports/ path will be usable for run-scoped evidence — proposed in design doc §6 and PRD Section 6.3, to be verified in S5
Archon's workflow validator and bundled-defaults infrastructure can accommodate a new default workflow — implied by AC1 and AC2, testable once S1 lands
technical_reality: V1 YAML is ~1116 lines with 9 nodes using string-based completion signals via <promise> tags — confirmed by inspection
V1 stores plans at .claude/archon/plans/{slug}.plan.md — confirmed in create-plan node prompt
V1 uses fresh_context: true for stateless per-task implement iterations — confirmed
Codex red lines prohibit per-node hooks, mcp, skills, agents, allowed_tools, denied_tools, and Claude-only fields — confirmed in SKILL.md
Design doc recommends 7 slices in the same order as the PRD — confirmed
spec_gaps: The PRD does not specify what happens when a V2 run discovers that the selected slice is no longer independent after implementation starts — low risk given one-slice-per-run constraint
The PRD does not specify whether the operator handoff prompt's integration-branch field should be a required input or auto-detected — non-blocking for S1 which starts from dev
downstream_risks: S3 typed-gate work could stall if loop.ts schema is harder to extend than assumed — PRD mitigates this by defaulting to sentinel contracts
Plan-path migration in S2 is genuinely load-bearing: V1 YAML has at least 5 nodes that reference .claude/archon/plans/ — a partial migration would break the workflow
If the one-slice boundary is not enforced tightly in the workflow YAML, V2 could drift into being a hidden campaign orchestrator
